official_primary_findings.title: MOFCOM/MOST Announcement 2026 No.48
facts: Public consultation (Oct 16-Nov 15, 2026) proposes 40 technology additions in AI, biomedicine and photovoltaics; AI comprises 23 technologies involving large models, agents, compute clusters and information processing.
Announcement says technologies already in public domain through open-source release or academic publication are outside management scope.

From Oct 16 until the revised Catalogue formally takes effect, exporters must register before exporting technologies listed in the announcement. Covered circumstances include transfer of technology ownership abroad, licensing domestic technology for foreign use, domestic ownership/controller becoming foreign, and other cases MOFCOM specifies; incomplete exports already underway are included.

official_primary_findings.title: MOFCOM spokesperson Q&A on Catalogue revision
facts: The Q&A says the determination turns on whether restricted technology is transferred from inside China to outside China; it describes the AI scope as limited and says most AI technologies remain freely exportable.

For restricted large-model technology, overseas local deployment is within technology-export management; Q&A says API calls, app/web interaction, SaaS, and lightweight local-edge deployment are outside large-model technology-export management. It says overseas self-owned-cloud deployment may qualify for automatic licensing in lower-risk cases.
The proposed measures are not a finding that Kimi K3.1 exists, is restricted, or would require a license/registration.

gaps: The Wccftech article body was not obtained (redirect returned HTTP 400). No direct Moonshot statement about Kimi K3.1 was captured in this three-source pass. Announcement attachment with detailed technology indicators was not retrieved; the announcement page and Q&A do not establish whether any particular Moonshot model falls within a listed item. Do not infer blanket treatment, K3.1 existence, or model-specific impact.
